newsitem.title: UK: Top aide of Prince Charles to quit early next year.
newsitem.headline: Top aide of Prince Charles to quit early next year.

text.p: Prince Charles's private secretary, Richard Aylard, has resigned, a spokeswoman in the prince's office said on Friday.
The decision of the 44-year-old former Royal Navy officer was mutally agreed with the heir-to-the-throne.
Aylard, who has been employed by Charles for 11 years and worked his way up to become the prince's closest aide, will leave the job early next year.
"It is a mutual decision," a palace spokeswoman said.
"His contract as private secretary was for five years and he has passed that. He always said that at some stage he would leave. Both the prince and Aylard feel the time is right for a change."
No successor has been chosen yet, she added.
Aylard, married with two children, announced in May that he and his wife had agreed to divorce.
His departure will mark a new era for the prince whose own divorce from Princess Diana, after 15 years of marriage, became final in August.

Aylard supported Charles throughout the turbulent divorce. But many of the prince's supporters hold the aide responsible for Charles's negative image after Aylard advised him to take part in a controversial television interview in which he admitted that he had committed adultery.

The admission of the prince's relationship with his long-time love Camilla Parker Bowles was followed by Diana's subsequent television interview in which she also confessed to breaking her marriage vows.
